# The provenance file on Zmey Gorynych

*Catalogue entry — Zmey Gorynych. Every claim below carries its chain of custody.*

## Provenance

**1. The attestation.** **—**, from the tradition's own record. On record: Bylina 'Dobrynya Nikitich and Zmey Gorynych', in the Kireevsky collection of byliny (recorded 1860s; ed. Barsov), A. N. Afanas'ev, Narodnye russkie skazki (1855–63), Kirsha Danilov, Drevnie rossiiskie stikhotvoreniia (mid-18th c. manuscript collection of byliny), V. Ia. Propp, Russian Epic Studies (1958).

**2. The narrative record.** **Dobrynya Rides to the Mountains** — In the bylina of Dobrynya Nikitich and Zmey Gorynych, recorded by the nineteenth-century collectors of the Kireevsky circle, the hero's mother warns him never to ride to the Sorochinsky mountains, for the fire-breathing serpent holds them.  The young hero rides anyway. **The Second Battle and the Wet Hat** — The dragon keeps neither his word nor his fear.  He seizes Zabava, niece of Prince Vladimir, and carries her to his mountain.

**3. The physical record.** No monument names Zmey Gorynych; the evidence is textual and pictorial rather than excavated. The dragon lives first in manuscripts — Kirsha Danilov's mid-eighteenth-century collection, the Kireevsky recordings of the 1860s, and the later Gil'ferding expedition collections from the Russian north. He lives second in the folk image: lubok woodcuts of the dragon fight sold at fairs from the seventeenth century onward, and the iconographic type of St George and the Dragon, which popular art quietly converted into Dobrynya's battle. Medieval Russian church sculpture and manuscript margins supply the serpent of Genesis and the dragon of the Apocalypse — the visual stock from which the bylina's Gorynych was assembled. The most vivid material witness is the most recent: the towering three-headed puppet built for Aleksandr Ptushko's film Ilya Muromets (1956), still the most-seen Gorynych ever made.

**4. The current holding.** The temple at [/zmeygorynych/](/zmeygorynych/), classified Tier 2. Tier-2 here means one preserved truth — not less important, just singular. The temple shows it and names it.

**5. The documented resonances.** **Defense, Military & Security**, **Agriculture, Food & Harvest**, **Gaming, Fantasy & Entertainment IP** — seats argued and weighted in the [pattern atlas](/patterns/), read through the myths in this temple's [Resonance File](/zmeygorynych/blog/resonance/).

**6. The continuing record.** The byliny are still sung — by folk ensembles in the Russian north and by animators in Moscow — and Zmey Gorynych remains their star monster.  His name is the Russian byword for any three-headed menace, from political caricature to sports mascots; 'Gorynych' alone summons the whole image of fire, mountains, and tribute.
